summary: The note surveys the autumn farm-to-table movement, focusing on Green Valley and its surrounding region. It covers a weekly Harvest Festival market, sustainable farming at Harris Homestead, seasonal cooking at Azure Farmhouse Restaurant, school education programs, local economic benefits, and environmental stewardship. The central argument is that local sourcing and seasonal eating strengthen communities, economies and the environment.
one_line: An autumn 2023 overview of the farm-to-table movement in Green Valley, covering markets, farming methods, restaurants, education, economics and sustainability.
key_facts: Green Valley launched a weekly Harvest Festival market on September 5, 2023, held every Saturday morning, rain or shine.
Sarah Johnson, a local agriculture advocate, organized the Green Valley Harvest Festival.
Jim Carter, a local apple grower, offers samples of his heritage apple varieties at the market.
Emily Harris of Harris Homestead uses planting by the almanac, organic pest control and crop rotation, and gave a tour of her polyculture fields on October 10, 2023.
Harris Homestead grows butternut squash, kale and a variety of root vegetables.
Chef Ricardo Lopez of the Azure Farmhouse Restaurant is known for his autumn menu and signature roasted acorn squash stuffed with wild rice and cranberries.
Azure Farmhouse hosted a full-house cooking class on September 25, 2023 on fall staples such as pears and sweet potatoes.
On September 15, 2023, the county's agricultural extension office and local schools launched a 'Harvest of the Month' program for children.
Nutritionist Margaret Freeman argues food literacy should start early, and school gardens let students take part in growing food.
The Urban Food Policy Institute's analysis of Green Valley's economy, provided October 20, 2023, found that money spent locally circulates within the community multiple times.
Artisanal butcher David Thomson partners with nearby livestock farmers and reports a surge in clients seeking locally sourced meats.

Dr. Helen Nguyen spoke at the Green Valley Environmental Conference on September 30, 2023, citing reduced transportation distances, support for small farms and biodiversity conservation as benefits of farm-to-table.
